checks.details: Five deterministic 3600x2260 captures at solver tick 3000 on d753926, covering first person at 90 and 140 km/h, first person in snowfall, dawn and thunderstorm. Retained as artifacts/mac_probe/look_*.png. The first-person set is the evidence for the new record; thunderstorm and the first-person snowfall frame extend the precipitation record; dawn is the lighting control added to the sky-ambient record. Rain was reviewed in the same pass and produced no new record.

The probe now applies the ordinary --first-person game argument after start_run, which main.gd only applies on its benchmark path. A first attempt without this produced a chase-view capture, so the option is verified by the close view actually appearing in look_fp_day.png.
status ok, no unavailable tasks, fifteen visual records parse with ready status and the single depends_on edge still resolves.
Backlog authoring plus a test-harness option that only selects an existing camera view. No runtime code path changes for players.

outstanding_acceptance: Authoring only. Nothing here is implemented or dispatched; each record's own human acceptance remains pending with its work.
The first-person speed-sensation question is recorded inside the new task as a related but separately owned concern, deliberately not folded into it. It has no record of its own yet.
Every capture in this pass was a held-speed straight tuck. Turning, jumping, landing and crash handovers in first person were not reviewed.
